newsitem.title: ITALY: S&P rates Bologna city foreign debt AA, neg outlook.
newsitem.headline: S&P rates Bologna city foreign debt AA, neg outlook.

text.p: Standard & Poor's Corp said on Tuesday it had assigned an AA counterparty rating to the Italian municipality (Comune) of Bologna's long-term foreign currency debt with a negative outlook with respect to that of the Italian Republic.

S&P said in a statement received in Milan it had assigned an A-1+ rating to short term foreign currency debt. For long term lira debt it assigned an AA+ rating and A-1+ for short term lira debt, with a stable outlook.
S&P said it based its rating on the "rich and diversified economy of the city and on its good financial performance."
It said Bologna had planned an important series of investments for the period 1996-99, particularly in the transport sector, which will be largely financed by state transfers and divestments.
"Given the discretional nature of these investments, the city's attention will be focused on maintaining a high rate of self-financing in order to limit the recourse to indebtedness.
"The direct debt burden, which for Bologna today represents a moderate 43 percent of total revenues, could increase to 50 percent in 1999, which would be perfectly reasonable," it said.
S&P said the favourable forecasts for economic growth and the high quality of city managers should allow Bologna to maintain a good financial performance and a moderate level of indebtedness.
